newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers little changed, quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers little changed, quiet trade.

text.p: Dirty tanker rates were little changed across the board in quiet trade on Thursday, brokers said.

In the Middle East the 1975-built Stena Continent was reported fixed for Coastal from Mina al-Bakr in Iraq to the U.S. Gulf at W50. The rate was typical for Middle East/U.S. very large crude carriers (VLCCs) with no special premium for Iraq, they said.
Some brokers detected a firmer tone in Middle East/Singapore VLCCs and put the rate at W52.5, up from W50. But all agreed the Middle East was quiet, with trips to Japan remaining at about W65/66.5.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs were steady at W67.5 or a couple of points higher for modern ships, with 130,000 tonners at W90.
The transatlantic sector was dormant with no VLCC fixtures seen, and the Mediterranean 130,000 tonne market was also torpid.
The cross-Med 80,000 tonne sector was more active, but the supply/demand balance was little changed and cargoes were still fixed at W125, or W130 for a quality ship, brokers said.
In the Caribbean, the only 70,000 tonne crude fixture was done at W115, little changed from W117.5/115 on Wednesday and 50,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes were quiet and unchanged at W170/175.
